question: Does the dead-code cleanup preserve runtime contracts while keeping the new Vulture gate precise?

findings.description: Global Vulture ignored names can suppress future unrelated findings.
findings.evidence: pyproject.toml:52 ignores cls, exc_info, param, query, variables, and url_vars across every configured source file.
findings.analysis: These names currently correspond to framework and protocol signatures, but Vulture applies ignore_names by identifier rather than declaration site. A future unused local or parameter with one of the same common names would not be reported.
findings.recommendation: Rename signature parameters that have no keyword-name contract with an underscore, retaining only the unavoidable url_vars ignore or a comparably narrow suppression.
findings.rationale: Keep the dead-code gate sensitive by suppressing only signature names that cannot be renamed without changing their keyword contract.

dispatch.outcome: The design and task plan now rename safely-renamable signature parameters and retain only the url_vars keyword-contract suppression.

recommendations.rationale: The final implementation retains only justified Vulture exceptions, removes confirmed unused state, and passes all required checks.
